steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mercury is the smallest planet, closest to the Sun, with no atmosphere and extreme temperature variations

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Venus has a thick CO2 atmosphere causing a runaway greenhouse effect; it rotates retrograde

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Earth is the only planet known to support life, with liquid water and a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mars has a thin CO2 atmosphere, the largest volcano (Olympus Mons) and canyon (Valles Marineris) in the Solar System

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Which planet has the strongest greenhouse effect and why? | Q: Why does Uranus appear blue-green? | Q: What causes Mercury's extreme temperature range?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Venus — its thick CO2 atmosphere traps heat, raising surface temperature to about 460°C. | Methane in its atmosphere absorbs red light and reflects blue-green light. | Mercury has virtually no atmosphere to retain heat, so the sunlit side reaches ~430°C while the dark side drops to ~−180°C.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use comparative language: 'whereas', 'compared to', 'in contrast to' Know at least one unique feature per planet — exam questions often ask about specific planets Venus is sometimes called Earth's 'twin' due to similar size, but conditions are very different For Edexcel, be prepared to compare and contrast terrestrial vs giant planets in a table
